findings.issue_text: FlusherProcess.__call__ was never updated for the new shards argument; spawned flusher processes crash on startup with TypeError (takes 6 positional arguments but 7 were given), causing the process-spans consumer to crash-loop via _ensure_processes_alive/MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS in process mode (produce_to_pipe=None), and this path is untested since new tests only use thread mode

--flusher-processes CLI option is parsed but never forwarded to ProcessSpansStrategyFactory in build_consumer, so the value is silently dropped in **options; the effective default becomes one flusher process per shard (opposite of the help text 'Defaults to 1'), silently multiplying flusher processes each with its own Redis client and Kafka producer, with no way for operators to tune it back down

Hung flusher threads are never terminated: for threads (produce_to_pipe set), process.kill() is skipped by the isinstance guard, the AttributeError is swallowed, and _create_process_for_shards starts a new thread for the same shards, permanently leaking hung threads holding Redis connections/producers and risking concurrent flushing of the same shards if a hung thread unhangs

Comma-joined shard tag corrupts DogStatsD tags: shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards)) produces tags like shard:0,2 which DogStatsD parses as shard:0 plus a bogus bare tag 2, silently truncating shard attribution to the first shard of each process

record_stored_segments() is now called once per process buffer per submit (for buffer in self.buffers.values()) instead of once per submit on the single shared buffer, inflating stored-segments accounting/metrics by the number of flusher processes

The added settle time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op lambda, so the test still depends on exactly the race the sleep was meant to close (the thread can observe stopped and exit between the drift change and its next flush)

SpanFlusher.terminate() is not updated in the diff; if its pre-existing implementation references the removed self.process (instead of self.processes), arroyo's forceful shutdown will raise AttributeError

P2: join() in flusher.py breaks out of the entire process loop once the deadline expires without calling terminate() on the current or any remaining flusher processes, so the hard-kill backstop that previously always ran can be skipped (e.g., if next_step.join(timeout) consumes the full timeout, zero processes are waited on or terminated), letting hung flushers keep producing to Kafka and holding Redis connections after shutdown
P2: When timeout=None in join(), waits are sequential so total shutdown time becomes the sum of per-process exit times rather than the max

P3: submit() in flusher.py has an N+1 shape — it loops over self.buffers calling record_stored_segments() and get_memory_info() once per flusher process/buffer instead of once per submit, multiplying potential Redis round-trips and sampling counter increments by the flusher process count

P3: Shard-tagged metrics (spans.buffer.flusher.produce, spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes, and spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy emitted once per shard per unhealthy poll) multiply time-series cardinality on hot flush-loop metrics, and the inconsistent tag key (shard vs shards in wait_produce) splits series further

P3: flusher_processes=None default in the factory/SpanFlusher silently changes resource footprint from 1 process to one-process-per-shard for non-CLI callers (each spawn is a full interpreter re-import with its own Kafka producer and Redis connection pool), and max_processes or ... conflates an explicit 0 with 'unlimited'

isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) check in _ensure_processes_alive() is always False for SpawnProcess instances, so process.kill() never executes; hung flusher processes are never killed and replacements run concurrently on the same shards, risking duplicate segment production, process leaks, and shared health-check state that can blind the health check to the replacement's hangs
join() deadline break exits the loop entirely once the deadline is exhausted, abandoning all remaining processes without waiting on or terminating them
process.terminate() in join() is guarded by the same always-False isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) check, so even the process that is reached is never force-terminated (pre-existing)
--flusher-processes is unvalidated: an explicit 0 is treated like None and silently produces one process per shard, while negative values crash with a cryptic KeyError at consumer startup

Inconsistent metric tag key: spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes are tagged 'shard' while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce is tagged 'shards', so dashboards/alerts aggregating by that tag silently miss the wait_produce series
test_basic relies on a fixed time.sleep(0.1) for the flusher thread to notice the drift change and flush before step.join() sets stopped, making the test flake-prone under CI load

New test test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts internal structure (process counts, shard sum) and never exercises actual data flow — no message submitted, no segment flushed, no Kafka payload inspected — so the multi-process flushing feature has zero behavioral/end-to-end coverage and cannot catch duplicate span production, bad shard distribution (e.g., all 4 shards on one process), or a flusher thread crashing at runtime

Rewritten health-monitoring/restart logic (_ensure_processes_alive, _create_process_for_shards) has zero test coverage: no test kills or hangs a process to verify only the affected process restarts, it's recreated with the correct shard subset, RuntimeError is raised after MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS (message format changed, silently breaking alerting), or restart counter/healthy-since reset behavior

time.sleep(0.1) added in test_basic is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched to a no-op lambda at the start of the test, so the added synchronization does nothing and the test still depends on a race between the flusher thread completing a poll/flush cycle after current_drift.value = 9000 and step.join() setting stopped — the flakiness it was meant to fix is not fixed

In thread mode (produce_to_pipe set), hang detection in _ensure_processes_alive skips kill() for threading.Thread but then starts a new thread on the same shards via _create_process_for_shards without stopping the old hung thread, resulting in two flushers racing on the same shard buffer with possible duplicate segment production; the old code at least failed loudly with AttributeError on Thread.kill

No validation or edge-case test for --flusher-processes <= 0: a negative value makes num_processes negative, range(negative) is empty, buffers are empty, submit() never raises MessageRejected, and _ensure_processes_alive can never restart anything — the consumer runs 'healthy' while segments accumulate in Redis and are never flushed; with 0, max_processes or len(...) silently means one process per shard, the opposite of what was requested

Inconsistent metric tag names between flusher timers: spans.buffer.flusher.produce is tagged {"shard": shard_tag} while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce is tagged {"shards": shard_tag} (plural), so dashboards/alerts joining on the shard tag across these metrics will silently miss series

Hung flusher thread is replaced but never stopped: in `_ensure_processes_alive`, `process.kill()` is only called inside `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` while `_create_process_for_shards(...)` is called unconditionally; in the `produce_to_pipe` path the process is a `threading.Thread` that cannot be killed, so on a `hang` detection the old hung thread keeps running against the old `shard_buffer` while a new thread starts on a fresh buffer, producing duplicate flushers polling the same Redis shards, duplicate segment production to Kafka/pipe, and both threads writing to the same shared `healthy_since`/`backpressure_since` `Value`s, corrupting health and backpressure signals (the old code failed loudly via `Thread.kill()` AttributeError; the new code silently duplicates work with no way to recover the stray thread)

The `buffer: SpansBuffer` constructor parameter's role silently changed from 'the buffer to flush' to merely a source of `buffer.assigned_shards`, and the flusher builds `SpansBuffer(shards)` per process with default construction arguments; nothing enforces these privately-constructed buffers are configured identically to the main buffer the factory creates (connection/cluster settings), so if they diverge the flusher children read the wrong Redis and silently stop flushing — a data-stall failure mode with no error signal

The diff contains no changes to `sentry/spans/buffer.py` yet depends on `assigned_shards` and a shards-accepting constructor, so the critical invariant that a fresh `SpansBuffer(shard_subset)` sees exactly the same Redis state as the main buffer lives across PR boundaries with no test or assertion enforcing it; per-submit accounting also now scales with process count (`record_stored_segments()` + `get_memory_info()` once per buffer instead of once total), with equivalence to the old single-buffer accounting depending on buffer internals not shown

Inconsistent defaults for `flusher_processes`: `flusher_processes: int | None = None` maps to `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (one spawn process per shard) while the CLI option documents and defaults to 1; any construction path bypassing CLI wiring (scripts, tests, future consumers) silently gets N spawn processes per consumer instead of 1, and `--flusher-processes 0` is silently coerced to 'unlimited' by the `or` — should pick one explicit default and validate `> 0`

Dead code: `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) is newly added in this diff but has no callers — both call sites (`_create_processes`, `_ensure_processes_alive`) use the plural `_create_process_for_shards`, and no external caller can exist for a brand-new private method; additionally `if not process: continue` in `_ensure_processes_alive` is unreachable since `self.processes` values are always live Process/Thread objects, never None/falsy — dead code in concurrency-management code misleads readers into assuming restart-per-shard semantics exist

Inconsistent metric tag keys: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` are tagged `{"shard": shard_tag}` while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged `{"shards": shard_tag}` — identical comma-joined values under two different keys, so tag-based dashboards/alerts and future per-shard aggregation will silently miss one of the series; standardize on one key

Misleading docstring/comments about the new process model: the class docstring claims 'Creates one process per shard for parallel processing' but the code creates `min(max_processes, len(shards))` processes with round-robin shard sharing (the common default `--flusher-processes 1` case is one process for all shards); the comment 'Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy' sits above a purely process-level check since `healthy_since` is per-process and updated once per cycle — per-shard health granularity does not exist, misdirecting anyone debugging health/restart behavior

Empty `assigned_shards` silently produces a zero-process flusher: `num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` yields 0 when the shard list is empty, making `_create_processes()` a no-op, `self.processes` empty, and `_ensure_processes_alive` iterate nothing — no flushing, no health monitoring, and no error forever; if shard assignment ever fails or arrives late this fails silently instead of loudly (the old code always ran one flusher loop)

Test race masked with `time.sleep(0.1)` in `tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:60–62`: the added `step.poll()` + sleep papers over a real ordering race where `join()` sets `stopped` before the flusher thread is guaranteed to have observed the drift change and produced, so the assertion depends on the thread winning a timing window; sleep-based synchronization will be flaky on loaded CI — the test (and shutdown path it exercises) needs a deterministic signal (e.g., wait until `messages` is populated or expose a flush-completed event) rather than a sleep

Production spawn path in flusher.py depends on SpansBuffer accepting a positional shard list and exposing an assigned_shards attribute, but no src/sentry/spans/buffer.py change appears in the diff; if the PR is complete as shown, every consumer startup (and the new tests) on the actual production path (produce_to_pipe is None → spawn) crashes with TypeError/AttributeError

Spawn-pickling of SpansBuffer's shard restriction is untested: nothing verifies whether the unpickled per-child buffer keeps the shard subset or reconstructs with all shards; if __reduce__/__getstate__ drops the restriction, every one of the N children flushes all shards, causing N× duplicate segment production to Kafka

--flusher-processes accepts negative values (e.g. -1, since click type=int allows it): -1 is truthy so num_processes = min(-1, N) = -1 and range(-1) creates zero processes; _ensure_processes_alive iterates nothing (RuntimeError can never fire), the backpressure loop never raises MessageRejected, and the memory guard is skipped, so the consumer ingests spans into Redis forever with nothing flushing them — silent data loss via TTL/eviction with zero errors, metrics, or log lines

--flusher-processes 0 is silently reinterpreted as 'auto' (one process per shard) because of the `0 or len(shards)` fallback, inconsistent with reasonable operator expectation, and no validation exists at the CLI or factory level

When hang detection fires on the thread path (produce_to_pipe set → threading.Thread), the stuck thread is never killed (the isinstance guard skips kill) while _create_process_for_shards immediately starts a replacement for the same shards; two live flushers race on buffer.flush, producing duplicate segments to Kafka and double-taking Redis processing markers, and each repeat detection stacks another thread until MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS trips — a silent failure where the old code failed loudly (AttributeError on Thread.kill); exposure limited to embedded/test/custom constructions since the shipped CLI path uses spawn processes where kill works

The only new multi-process test (test_flusher_processes_limit) asserts structure, not behavior: it never submits a message, never asserts a single span/segment is flushed, and constructs the flusher with produce_to_pipe (threads) so the production spawn/pickle path is never exercised; len(flusher.processes) == 2 and shard-map totals would stay green even if children flushed the wrong shards, all shards, or nothing at all, leaving the headline feature (parallel flushing with correct shard ownership) with zero behavioral coverage

join() can abandon all flusher processes without terminate(): the deadline is computed before next_step.join(timeout), which receives the full timeout; if the committer/producer consumes it, remaining_time <= 0 breaks on the first iteration so no process is waited on or terminated (regression vs. the old always-terminate behavior); orphaned daemons keep flushing/producing, and a genuinely hung process that later recovers resumes flushing shards that may already belong to a successor strategy after rebalance, creating a duplicate-production window

The 'synchronization' sleep added to test_basic is a no-op: monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None) patches time.sleep globally, so the subsequent time.sleep(0.1) ('Give flusher threads time to process after drift change') invokes the patched lambda and does nothing; the test passes only due to the tight flusher loop plus join() semantics, and the comment documents a synchronization guarantee that doesn't exist

submit() now calls record_stored_segments() and get_memory_info() on N separate buffer instances per message, multiplying per-submit Redis round-trips N× and emitting gauge metrics N×, changing dashboard semantics

Cross-buffer memory aggregation may double-count shared Redis servers: if get_memory_info dedupes by physical Redis server per buffer, summing across buffers counts servers touched by multiple groups multiple times, making used/available a weighted average that can underestimate pressure so memory backpressure fires late, risking Redis OOM/eviction (contingent on buffer.py internals not in the diff — flagged for verification, not asserted)

This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FlusherProcess.__call__ was never updated for the new shards argument; spawned flusher processes crash on startup with TypeError (takes 6 positional arguments but 7 were given), causing the process-spans consumer to crash-loop via _ensure_processes_alive/MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS in process mode (produce_to_pipe=None), and this path is untested since new tests only use thread mode

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, both process mode (`produce_to_pipe is None`) and thread mode pass `args=(shards, stopped, current_drift, backpressure_since, healthy_since, produce_to_pipe)` to a target created as `partial(SpanFlusher.main, shard_buffer)`. The updated `SpanFlusher.main` signature explicitly includes `shards` as the first arg after `buffer`, so the bound `buffer` + 6 passed args match (no “6 vs 7” positional mismatch shown in this diff). Also, the finding references `FlusherProcess.__call__`, which does not appear anywhere in the provided diff, so the claimed crash source is not verifiable from this PR diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: --flusher-processes CLI option is parsed but never forwarded to ProcessSpansStrategyFactory in build_consumer, so the value is silently dropped in **options; the effective default becomes one flusher process per shard (opposite of the help text 'Defaults to 1'), silently multiplying flusher processes each with its own Redis client and Kafka producer, with no way for operators to tune it back down

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `--flusher-processes` click option (named `flusher_processes`) and wires a new `flusher_processes` argument through `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` into `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`. However, the finding hinges on `build_consumer` not forwarding the parsed CLI value into `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory`—and `build_consumer` is not shown/modified anywhere in this diff, so that claim cannot be verified from the provided changes. If the value is forwarded, `max_processes=1` would correctly limit flusher processes; the “silently dropped” part is not established by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hung flusher threads are never terminated: for threads (produce_to_pipe set), process.kill() is skipped by the isinstance guard, the AttributeError is swallowed, and _create_process_for_shards starts a new thread for the same shards, permanently leaking hung threads holding Redis connections/producers and risking concurrent flushing of the same shards if a hung thread unhangs

adjudication.rationale: In thread mode (when `produce_to_pipe` is not `None`), `_create_process_for_shards` creates a `threading.Thread` (see `make_process = threading.Thread`). In `_ensure_processes_alive`, if a thread is considered unhealthy due to the `healthy_since` timeout (`cause = "hang"`), the restart path runs. However, termination is guarded by `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()`, so threads are never stopped. The code then unconditionally calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, starting a new thread for the same shards while the old (hung) thread can remain alive and untracked (it is overwritten in `self.processes[...]`). `join()` also only waits/terminates the currently tracked threads/processes, so leaked hung threads would persist, potentially continuing to flush the same shards concurrently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Comma-joined shard tag corrupts DogStatsD tags: shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards)) produces tags like shard:0,2 which DogStatsD parses as shard:0 plus a bogus bare tag 2, silently truncating shard attribution to the first shard of each process

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a tag value built as `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))` and then passes it into `metrics.timer(..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` / `metrics.timing(..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`. This means tag values can contain commas (e.g. "0,2"). Whether that *actually* corrupts DogStatsD parsing depends on how `sentry.utils.metrics` encodes tags for the backend (not shown in the diff), but commas in tag values are a concrete compatibility risk and could lead to misleading per-shard attribution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_stored_segments() is now called once per process buffer per submit (for buffer in self.buffers.values()) instead of once per submit on the single shared buffer, inflating stored-segments accounting/metrics by the number of flusher processes

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `submit()` from a single call `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` to a loop over all per-process shard buffers: `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()` (SpanFlusher.submit). That means the method is now invoked N times per submit where N=`len(self.buffers)`/`num_processes`. However, the claim that this *necessarily* inflates stored-segment accounting/metrics by the number of flusher processes is not directly verifiable from the diff because `record_stored_segments()` implementation/metric semantics are not shown; if each buffer only reports its shard subset, summing may be correct. Still, the increased call multiplicity is a concrete, diff-grounded concern that could affect accounting/metrics or overhead and should be reviewed.

SpanFlusher.terminate() is not updated in the diff; if its pre-existing implementation references the removed self.process (instead of self.processes), arroyo's forceful shutdown will raise AttributeError

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows SpanFlusher was refactored from a single `self.process` to a `self.processes` dict, and `join()` was updated to iterate processes and call `terminate()` per-process. However, there is no `SpanFlusher.terminate()` method shown in the diff (added/modified/removed), so the claim that an existing `terminate()` still references removed `self.process` cannot be verified from this patch alone.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that join() exits the loop when the deadline expires and therefore may not call terminate() on the current or remaining flusher processes, allowing them to keep running after shutdown. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: When timeout=None in join(), waits are sequential so total shutdown time becomes the sum of per-process exit times rather than the max

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), the code loops over processes and waits on each in turn, but all processes are already running concurrently after `self.stopped.value = True`. Waiting sequentially does not make total shutdown time the sum of per-process exit times; it will still generally be bounded by the time until the last process exits (i.e., ~max of exit times), since other processes can finish while waiting on the first. The diff does not show any behavior where later processes only begin exiting after earlier ones are waited on.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: submit() in flusher.py has an N+1 shape — it loops over self.buffers calling record_stored_segments() and get_memory_info() once per flusher process/buffer instead of once per submit, multiplying potential Redis round-trips and sampling counter increments by the flusher process count

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit()` the diff changes from single-buffer calls to iterating over all per-process buffers: `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()` and later `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())` (flusher.py). Since `self.buffers` is now one `SpansBuffer` per flusher process/shard-group, these operations will run once per buffer on every `submit()`, scaling Redis reads/counters with `num_processes`. This is a concrete perf/overhead concern introduced by the change, but not a clear correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Shard-tagged metrics (spans.buffer.flusher.produce, spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes, and spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy emitted once per shard per unhealthy poll) multiply time-series cardinality on hot flush-loop metrics, and the inconsistent tag key (shard vs shards in wait_produce) splits series further

P3: flusher_processes=None default in the factory/SpanFlusher silently changes resource footprint from 1 process to one-process-per-shard for non-CLI callers (each spawn is a full interpreter re-import with its own Kafka producer and Redis connection pool), and max_processes or ... conflates an explicit 0 with 'unlimited'

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the new parameter `max_processes` defaults to `None`, and is immediately normalized via `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`. This means callers that previously constructed a single background process/thread (old code called `_create_process()` once) will now, by default, create `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` processes/threads (one per shard) unless they explicitly pass a limit. That’s a concrete, diff-introduced change in resource footprint for non-CLI callers. Also, using `or` conflates an explicit `0` with `None` (i.e., `0` becomes “unlimited”/per-shard), which is a real edge-case in the new logic. This is a significant behavioral/architecture concern but not a directly provable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) check in _ensure_processes_alive() is always False for SpawnProcess instances, so process.kill() never executes; hung flusher processes are never killed and replacements run concurrently on the same shards, risking duplicate segment production, process leaks, and shared health-check state that can blind the health check to the replacement's hangs
matched_golden_ids: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify that flusher processes are SpawnProcess instances created via the spawn context, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` evaluates false (on POSIX), preventing `process.kill()` from running and leaving hung processes unhandled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: join() deadline break exits the loop entirely once the deadline is exhausted, abandoning all remaining processes without waiting on or terminating them

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the loop over `self.processes` computes `remaining_time` and does `if remaining_time <= 0: break` (new code in `flusher.py`). That `break` exits the *entire* `for process_index, process in self.processes.items()` loop, so any processes not yet visited will neither be waited on (`while process.is_alive() ...`) nor terminated (`process.terminate()`), even though the method has already set `self.stopped.value = True`. This can leave remaining flusher processes running past shutdown when a timeout is provided and exhausted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: process.terminate() in join() is guarded by the same always-False isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) check, so even the process that is reached is never force-terminated (pre-existing)

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the termination is guarded by `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.terminate()`. Processes are created via `self.mp_context.Process` (spawn context), which returns a `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` that is a subclass of `multiprocessing.Process`, so the check is not “always-false”. It correctly skips termination only for the thread case (`threading.Thread`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: --flusher-processes is unvalidated: an explicit 0 is treated like None and silently produces one process per shard, while negative values crash with a cryptic KeyError at consumer startup

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `--flusher-processes` click option with `type=int` but no validation for non-positive values. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means an explicit `0` is treated as falsy and replaced with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, silently creating one process per shard. For negative values (e.g. `-1`), `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` becomes negative, producing an empty `process_to_shards_map` (`range(self.num_processes)`), and then `process_index = i % self.num_processes` followed by `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(...)` will raise a `KeyError` during initialization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent metric tag key: spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes are tagged 'shard' while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce is tagged 'shards', so dashboards/alerts aggregating by that tag silently miss the wait_produce series
matched_golden_ids: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same inconsistency in metric tag keys ('shard' vs 'shards') across SpanFlusher flush metrics, and notes the resulting aggregation/dashboard/alerting miss for the wait_produce series—matching the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_basic relies on a fixed time.sleep(0.1) for the flusher thread to notice the drift change and flush before step.join() sets stopped, making the test flake-prone under CI load

adjudication.rationale: In `test_basic`, the added `time.sleep(0.1)` does not actually introduce a fixed wait because earlier the test does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, which patches `time.sleep` in the `time` module. The later `time.sleep(0.1)` therefore becomes a no-op, so the test is not relying on a real 0.1s delay that could flake under CI load as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New test test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts internal structure (process counts, shard sum) and never exercises actual data flow — no message submitted, no segment flushed, no Kafka payload inspected — so the multi-process flushing feature has zero behavioral/end-to-end coverage and cannot catch duplicate span production, bad shard distribution (e.g., all 4 shards on one process), or a flusher thread crashing at runtime

adjudication.rationale: In `tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py`, the new `test_flusher_processes_limit` only constructs the strategy (`fac.create_with_partitions(...)`) and asserts internal state (`len(flusher.processes) == 2`, `flusher.num_processes == 2`, and that `process_to_shards_map` covers 4 shards). It never submits any messages to the step, never causes `SpanFlusher.main` to flush segments/produce to Kafka (it uses `produce_to_pipe=messages.append` but never asserts on `messages`), and thus provides no behavioral coverage for the newly added multi-process/shard-distribution flushing logic in `SpanFlusher` (e.g., production correctness, runtime crashes, per-shard behavior). This is a concrete test-gap concern, not a verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Rewritten health-monitoring/restart logic (_ensure_processes_alive, _create_process_for_shards) has zero test coverage: no test kills or hangs a process to verify only the affected process restarts, it's recreated with the correct shard subset, RuntimeError is raised after MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS (message format changed, silently breaking alerting), or restart counter/healthy-since reset behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff substantially rewrites flusher lifecycle/health logic from a single `self.process` to multiple processes with per-process state (`process_to_shards_map`, `process_healthy_since`, `process_backpressure_since`, `process_restarts`) and new restart behavior in `_ensure_processes_alive()` plus `_create_process_for_shards()`. The added tests (`test_basic`, `test_flusher_processes_limit`, and the updated assertion in `test_flusher.py`) only validate basic flushing/backpressure wiring and that the process-count limit/shard distribution is set up; they do not exercise the new failure paths (process/thread not alive, hang via `healthy_since`, restarting only the affected shard-group, or the repeated-crash `RuntimeError` path). Given the nontrivial new logic, this is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: time.sleep(0.1) added in test_basic is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched to a no-op lambda at the start of the test, so the added synchronization does nothing and the test still depends on a race between the flusher thread completing a poll/flush cycle after current_drift.value = 9000 and step.join() setting stopped — the flakiness it was meant to fix is not fixed

In thread mode (produce_to_pipe set), hang detection in _ensure_processes_alive skips kill() for threading.Thread but then starts a new thread on the same shards via _create_process_for_shards without stopping the old hung thread, resulting in two flushers racing on the same shard buffer with possible duplicate segment production; the old code at least failed loudly with AttributeError on Thread.kill

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, when a flusher running in thread mode (i.e. `produce_to_pipe` set, so `process` is a `threading.Thread`) is deemed unhealthy (`hang` based on `process_healthy_since`), the code intentionally skips termination (`if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()`) and then unconditionally calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, which starts a *new* thread for the same shard set. The old unhealthy thread is not stopped or joined, and the `AttributeError`/inability to kill threads is now swallowed (`except (ValueError, AttributeError): pass`). This can leave two concurrent flush loops polling/producing for the same `shards` (each with its own `SpansBuffer(shards)`), plausibly causing duplicate segment production/races. This problematic behavior is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No validation or edge-case test for --flusher-processes <= 0: a negative value makes num_processes negative, range(negative) is empty, buffers are empty, submit() never raises MessageRejected, and _ensure_processes_alive can never restart anything — the consumer runs 'healthy' while segments accumulate in Redis and are never flushed; with 0, max_processes or len(...) silently means one process per shard, the opposite of what was requested

adjudication.rationale: The new `--flusher-processes` click option is an unconstrained `int` (no validation), and `SpanFlusher.__init__` uses `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. This makes `0` silently fall back to `len(...)` (opposite of “0 processes”), and a negative value stays negative/truthy. With `max_processes < 0`, `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` becomes negative, `process_to_shards_map` is built from `range(self.num_processes)` (empty), and then the shard distribution loop does `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)`, which will raise a `KeyError` for any non-empty `assigned_shards`. This is a real defect introduced/exposed by the diff, even though the finding’s later claimed “healthy but never flushes” behavior is not quite accurate given the likely crash.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent metric tag names between flusher timers: spans.buffer.flusher.produce is tagged {"shard": shard_tag} while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce is tagged {"shards": shard_tag} (plural), so dashboards/alerts joining on the shard tag across these metrics will silently miss series

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent metric tag keys for related timers in `SpanFlusher.main`: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` vs `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})`. This is a real, diff-grounded observability issue that can cause dashboards/alerts joining on a single tag name to miss series, but it does not affect core flushing correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hung flusher thread is replaced but never stopped: in `_ensure_processes_alive`, `process.kill()` is only called inside `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` while `_create_process_for_shards(...)` is called unconditionally; in the `produce_to_pipe` path the process is a `threading.Thread` that cannot be killed, so on a `hang` detection the old hung thread keeps running against the old `shard_buffer` while a new thread starts on a fresh buffer, producing duplicate flushers polling the same Redis shards, duplicate segment production to Kafka/pipe, and both threads writing to the same shared `healthy_since`/`backpressure_since` `Value`s, corrupting health and backpressure signals (the old code failed loudly via `Thread.kill()` AttributeError; the new code silently duplicates work with no way to recover the stray thread)

adjudication.rationale: In the `produce_to_pipe` path, `_create_process_for_shards` uses `threading.Thread` (see `make_process = threading.Thread`), but `_ensure_processes_alive` only calls `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. On a detected hang (`time.time() - self.process_healthy_since[process_index].value > max_unhealthy_seconds`), it unconditionally starts a replacement thread via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` without any mechanism to stop/join/terminate the old hung thread. Since both threads target the same shard list and share the same `mp_context.Value` objects (`process_backpressure_since[...]`, `process_healthy_since[...]`) within the same process, this can lead to multiple flushers concurrently polling/producing for the same shards and corrupting health/backpressure signaling. The prior code would at least raise an AttributeError on `Thread.kill()`; the new code silently allows duplication.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `buffer: SpansBuffer` constructor parameter's role silently changed from 'the buffer to flush' to merely a source of `buffer.assigned_shards`, and the flusher builds `SpansBuffer(shards)` per process with default construction arguments; nothing enforces these privately-constructed buffers are configured identically to the main buffer the factory creates (connection/cluster settings), so if they diverge the flusher children read the wrong Redis and silently stop flushing — a data-stall failure mode with no error signal

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the passed-in `buffer: SpansBuffer` is no longer retained/used for flushing (the prior `self.buffer = buffer` is removed). Instead, the flusher derives shard assignment from `buffer.assigned_shards` and then constructs new per-process buffers via `shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)` in `_create_process_for_shards`, passing those into `SpanFlusher.main`. The diff does not show any mechanism to ensure these newly constructed `SpansBuffer` instances inherit any non-shard configuration that might have existed on the original `buffer` (e.g., connection/client options), so this is a legitimate design/robustness concern grounded in the change, though whether it is an actual runtime defect depends on `SpansBuffer`’s implementation (not shown in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The diff contains no changes to `sentry/spans/buffer.py` yet depends on `assigned_shards` and a shards-accepting constructor, so the critical invariant that a fresh `SpansBuffer(shard_subset)` sees exactly the same Redis state as the main buffer lives across PR boundaries with no test or assertion enforcing it; per-submit accounting also now scales with process count (`record_stored_segments()` + `get_memory_info()` once per buffer instead of once total), with equivalence to the old single-buffer accounting depending on buffer internals not shown

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes SpanFlusher to instantiate new per-process buffers via `shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)` and to derive shard assignments from `buffer.assigned_shards`, without any corresponding changes shown to `SpansBuffer` itself. While we can’t verify from this diff whether `SpansBuffer` already supports a shards-list constructor and identical Redis semantics, the concern is diff-grounded: previously a single `buffer` instance was shared into the flusher; now multiple new `SpansBuffer` instances are created, so correctness/consistency depends on unseen buffer internals. Additionally, `submit()` now loops over `self.buffers.values()` to call `record_stored_segments()` and aggregates `get_memory_info()` across buffers, which makes accounting scale with process count and could change behavior if those calls aren’t strictly shard-local.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent defaults for `flusher_processes`: `flusher_processes: int | None = None` maps to `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (one spawn process per shard) while the CLI option documents and defaults to 1; any construction path bypassing CLI wiring (scripts, tests, future consumers) silently gets N spawn processes per consumer instead of 1, and `--flusher-processes 0` is silently coerced to 'unlimited' by the `or` — should pick one explicit default and validate `> 0`

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` defaults `flusher_processes` to `None` and passes it through as `max_processes` to `SpanFlusher`. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means `None` (and also `0`) results in `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` processes (one per shard after `self.num_processes = min(...)`). This is inconsistent with the new CLI option `--flusher-processes` which defaults to `1` and documents “Defaults to 1.” It also means `--flusher-processes 0` is silently treated as “unlimited/per-shard” due to the `or`. These behaviors are directly implied by the diff and can cause unexpectedly high process counts on non-CLI construction paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) is newly added in this diff but has no callers — both call sites (`_create_processes`, `_ensure_processes_alive`) use the plural `_create_process_for_shards`, and no external caller can exist for a brand-new private method; additionally `if not process: continue` in `_ensure_processes_alive` is unreachable since `self.processes` values are always live Process/Thread objects, never None/falsy — dead code in concurrency-management code misleads readers into assuming restart-per-shard semantics exist

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new private method `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` but there are no call sites in the shown changes: startup uses `_create_processes()` → `_create_process_for_shards(...)`, and restarts in `_ensure_processes_alive()` also call `_create_process_for_shards(...)`. Since it’s brand-new and private, an external caller is unlikely, so it is effectively dead code in this diff. Additionally, `_ensure_processes_alive()` contains `if not process: continue`, but `self.processes` is populated with `process = make_process(...)` objects and never assigned `None`/falsy values in the shown code, making that guard redundant/unreachable. These are maintainability/clarity issues rather than a demonstrated runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent metric tag keys: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` are tagged `{"shard": shard_tag}` while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged `{"shards": shard_tag}` — identical comma-joined values under two different keys, so tag-based dashboards/alerts and future per-shard aggregation will silently miss one of the series; standardize on one key

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce inconsistent metric tag keys: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use `shard`, while `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards` even though the value is the same comma-joined `shard_tag`. This won’t break runtime behavior, but it will fragment/skip series in tag-based dashboards and alerts and makes per-shard aggregation inconsistent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Misleading docstring/comments about the new process model: the class docstring claims 'Creates one process per shard for parallel processing' but the code creates `min(max_processes, len(shards))` processes with round-robin shard sharing (the common default `--flusher-processes 1` case is one process for all shards); the comment 'Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy' sits above a purely process-level check since `healthy_since` is per-process and updated once per cycle — per-shard health granularity does not exist, misdirecting anyone debugging health/restart behavior

adjudication.rationale: The updated class docstring in `SpanFlusher` says it "Creates one process per shard", but the implementation explicitly supports fewer processes than shards via `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` and then assigns shards round-robin into `process_to_shards_map`. So it is not always one-process-per-shard. Also, in `_ensure_processes_alive`, the comment "Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy" is misleading: the hang check is purely `time.time() - self.process_healthy_since[process_index].value > max_unhealthy_seconds`, and `healthy_since` is maintained per-process (updated once per loop in `main`), not per-shard. These are documentation/comment correctness issues rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Empty `assigned_shards` silently produces a zero-process flusher: `num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` yields 0 when the shard list is empty, making `_create_processes()` a no-op, `self.processes` empty, and `_ensure_processes_alive` iterate nothing — no flushing, no health monitoring, and no error forever; if shard assignment ever fails or arrives late this fails silently instead of loudly (the old code always ran one flusher loop)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make `SpanFlusher` create zero worker processes when `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` becomes `0`, then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` is `0`, so `process_to_shards_map`, `processes`, `buffers`, and the per-process health/backpressure dicts are all empty and `_create_processes()` is a no-op. As a result, `_ensure_processes_alive()` and the backpressure/memory checks iterate over empty collections and won’t raise/monitor anything. However, from the diff alone it’s not verifiable that an empty shard assignment is an error condition (it may be a valid “no partitions assigned” state where doing nothing is correct), and the claim about shards “arriving late” isn’t shown in this code. This is still a concrete edge-case introduced by the refactor that merits an explicit decision (assert/log/handle), but it’s not provably a correctness bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test race masked with `time.sleep(0.1)` in `tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:60–62`: the added `step.poll()` + sleep papers over a real ordering race where `join()` sets `stopped` before the flusher thread is guaranteed to have observed the drift change and produced, so the assertion depends on the thread winning a timing window; sleep-based synchronization will be flaky on loaded CI — the test (and shutdown path it exercises) needs a deterministic signal (e.g., wait until `messages` is populated or expose a flush-completed event) rather than a sleep

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `step.poll()` followed by `time.sleep(0.1)` in `test_basic` right after mutating `fac._flusher.current_drift.value` and before `step.join()`. That is a timing-based attempt to let the background flusher thread/process observe state and produce before shutdown, i.e., it’s nondeterministic synchronization. Moreover, in this same test the code still does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, so the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` is actually a no-op, underscoring that the test is relying on scheduling/order rather than a deterministic signal (e.g., waiting for `messages` to be populated). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test robustness concern rather than a proven production correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Production spawn path in flusher.py depends on SpansBuffer accepting a positional shard list and exposing an assigned_shards attribute, but no src/sentry/spans/buffer.py change appears in the diff; if the PR is complete as shown, every consumer startup (and the new tests) on the actual production path (produce_to_pipe is None → spawn) crashes with TypeError/AttributeError

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `flusher.py` now relies on `buffer.assigned_shards` (e.g. `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and iterating `for i, shard in enumerate(buffer.assigned_shards)`) and also instantiates per-process buffers via `SpansBuffer(shards)` in `_create_process_for_shards`. No corresponding `src/sentry/spans/buffer.py` change is shown, so the PR as presented introduces a new/changed API dependency on `SpansBuffer` that reviewers should verify exists; however, the claim that it *will* crash cannot be confirmed from this diff alone because `SpansBuffer`’s current constructor/attributes are not visible here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spawn-pickling of SpansBuffer's shard restriction is untested: nothing verifies whether the unpickled per-child buffer keeps the shard subset or reconstructs with all shards; if __reduce__/__getstate__ drops the restriction, every one of the N children flushes all shards, causing N× duplicate segment production to Kafka

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces per-process shard buffers created in the parent (`shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)`) and passed into a spawned child via `mp_context.Process` (`target = partial(SpanFlusher.main, shard_buffer)`). Whether `SpansBuffer`’s shard restriction survives spawn pickling is not verified anywhere in the added/updated tests: the new `test_flusher_processes_limit` sets `produce_to_pipe=messages.append`, which forces the threading path (not `multiprocessing.Process`), so it does not exercise pickling/unpickling of `SpansBuffer`. The claimed duplication failure mode depends on `SpansBuffer`’s pickle behavior, which is not shown in the diff, so it’s not a verifiable defect from this patch—but the lack of coverage for the new spawn-based shard isolation is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: --flusher-processes accepts negative values (e.g. -1, since click type=int allows it): -1 is truthy so num_processes = min(-1, N) = -1 and range(-1) creates zero processes; _ensure_processes_alive iterates nothing (RuntimeError can never fire), the backpressure loop never raises MessageRejected, and the memory guard is skipped, so the consumer ingests spans into Redis forever with nothing flushing them — silent data loss via TTL/eviction with zero errors, metrics, or log lines

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a Click option with `type=int` and no bounds, so negative values are possible. However, the claimed runtime behavior is not supported by the shown code: in `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` would become `-1` for `--flusher-processes=-1`, making `process_to_shards_map` empty (`range(-1)`), and then `process_index = i % self.num_processes` followed by `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)` would error (KeyError, since key 0 doesn't exist). So it would likely crash during initialization rather than silently running with “zero processes” and bypassing backpressure/memory guards as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: --flusher-processes 0 is silently reinterpreted as 'auto' (one process per shard) because of the `0 or len(shards)` fallback, inconsistent with reasonable operator expectation, and no validation exists at the CLI or factory level

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a CLI option `--flusher-processes` (type int, no validation) and threads it to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means a user-supplied `0` is treated as falsy and silently replaced with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, i.e. “auto/one per shard”. This is inconsistent with the CLI help text (“Maximum number… Defaults to 1.”) and there is no guard at the CLI or factory level to reject 0, so `--flusher-processes 0` yields surprising behavior introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: When hang detection fires on the thread path (produce_to_pipe set → threading.Thread), the stuck thread is never killed (the isinstance guard skips kill) while _create_process_for_shards immediately starts a replacement for the same shards; two live flushers race on buffer.flush, producing duplicate segments to Kafka and double-taking Redis processing markers, and each repeat detection stacks another thread until MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS trips — a silent failure where the old code failed loudly (AttributeError on Thread.kill); exposure limited to embedded/test/custom constructions since the shipped CLI path uses spawn processes where kill works

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, when a worker is deemed unhealthy it conditionally calls `process.kill()` only if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. For the `produce_to_pipe` path, workers are `threading.Thread` (created in `_create_process_for_shards`), so no termination happens; yet `_create_process_for_shards` is still invoked, starting a replacement thread for the same shard set. Nothing signals the old thread to stop (the shared `stopped` flag is only set in `join()`), so multiple live flushers can concurrently flush the same Redis shards and produce duplicates. This also changes prior behavior: the old code would attempt `self.process.kill()` unguarded and would likely raise on threads (failing loudly), whereas now it silently spawns replacements and increments restart counters until MAX is hit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The only new multi-process test (test_flusher_processes_limit) asserts structure, not behavior: it never submits a message, never asserts a single span/segment is flushed, and constructs the flusher with produce_to_pipe (threads) so the production spawn/pickle path is never exercised; len(flusher.processes) == 2 and shard-map totals would stay green even if children flushed the wrong shards, all shards, or nothing at all, leaving the headline feature (parallel flushing with correct shard ownership) with zero behavioral coverage

adjudication.rationale: In `tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py`, the new `test_flusher_processes_limit` only checks internal structure (`len(flusher.processes) == 2`, `process_to_shards_map` totals) and never submits messages or asserts any flushing/output behavior. It also constructs the factory with `produce_to_pipe=messages.append`, which in `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards` selects `threading.Thread` (`make_process = threading.Thread`) rather than the multiprocessing spawn/pickle path (`mp_context.Process`). As written, the test can pass even if shard ownership is wrong or nothing is flushed, so it provides no behavioral coverage for the new parallel shard-to-process flushing logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: join() can abandon all flusher processes without terminate(): the deadline is computed before next_step.join(timeout), which receives the full timeout; if the committer/producer consumes it, remaining_time <= 0 breaks on the first iteration so no process is waited on or terminated (regression vs. the old always-terminate behavior); orphaned daemons keep flushing/producing, and a genuinely hung process that later recovers resumes flushing shards that may already belong to a successor strategy after rebalance, creating a duplicate-production window

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, `deadline` is computed before `self.next_step.join(timeout)` but `next_step.join` is still given the full `timeout`. If `next_step.join` consumes most/all of that time, then in the subsequent loop `remaining_time <= 0` triggers `break`, which skips both waiting on and `terminate()`-ing any remaining multiprocessing flusher processes. This is a regression from the old code path where `terminate()` was unconditionally called after the wait loop, and can leave daemon flusher processes running beyond the strategy shutdown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'synchronization' sleep added to test_basic is a no-op: monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None) patches time.sleep globally, so the subsequent time.sleep(0.1) ('Give flusher threads time to process after drift change') invokes the patched lambda and does nothing; the test passes only due to the tight flusher loop plus join() semantics, and the comment documents a synchronization guarantee that doesn't exist
matched_golden_ids: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue correctly identifies that test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to a lambda that returns immediately, so the later time.sleep(0.1) meant to provide synchronization does not actually wait. This is the same underlying problem described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: submit() now calls record_stored_segments() and get_memory_info() on N separate buffer instances per message, multiplying per-submit Redis round-trips N× and emitting gauge metrics N×, changing dashboard semantics

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `SpanFlusher.submit()` from calling `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` and `list(self.buffer.get_memory_info())` once to iterating over `self.buffers.values()` and calling `record_stored_segments()` / `get_memory_info()` for each per-process `SpansBuffer` (created in `_create_process_for_shards`). This makes those operations run N times per submit where N=`len(self.buffers)`/`num_processes`. While the finding’s claims about Redis round-trips and gauge/dashboard semantics depend on `SpansBuffer` internals not shown here, the multiplicative per-submit behavior is directly introduced by the diff and is a concrete performance/observability concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cross-buffer memory aggregation may double-count shared Redis servers: if get_memory_info dedupes by physical Redis server per buffer, summing across buffers counts servers touched by multiple groups multiple times, making used/available a weighted average that can underestimate pressure so memory backpressure fires late, risking Redis OOM/eviction (contingent on buffer.py internals not in the diff — flagged for verification, not asserted)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes memory-pressure calculation from a single `self.buffer.get_memory_info()` to aggregating across multiple per-process `SpansBuffer` instances (`memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())` then `used = sum(...)`, `available = sum(...)`). If `get_memory_info()` reports overlapping/shared Redis servers across shard groups, this naive summation could double-count those servers and distort the used/available ratio. Whether that overlap can happen depends on `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` internals (not shown), so it’s a diff-grounded risk worth verifying rather than a provable defect from this diff alone.
